name: Digital advertising

naics.title: Media Streaming Distribution Services, Social Networks, and Other Media Networks

one_line: Sells advertisers access to online audiences across search, social, video and shopping sites. The money that funds most 'free' content.
sells: Targeted ad placements, sold by auction or negotiated deal
customers: Advertisers and the agencies that buy on their behalf
suppliers: The content and platforms that draw the audience, plus ad-tech plumbing, data and measurement

revenue.basis: industry (eMarketer forecast; total implied from company shares)
revenue.note: eMarketer's April 2026 forecast puts Meta at $243.5B (26.8%), Google at $239.5B (26.4%) and Amazon at $82.1B (9%); the ~$908B total is implied from those shares. GroupM puts 2026 global digital ad spend nearer $836B, so estimates vary. Digital is roughly two-thirds of all advertising (total ad market ~$1.3T, WARC/GroupM).

structure.why: Three firms - Meta, Google and Amazon - take about 62% of worldwide digital ad spending, and Meta is forecast to pass Google for the first time in 2026. A long tail of platforms and publishers splits the rest.
structure.hhi_note: Sum of squared shares of the six listed firms (eMarketer 2026 worldwide digital-ad shares). The fragmented ~26% tail (open-web publishers, ad networks, regional players) is excluded, so this is a lower bound.

econ: Increasing returns from data and scale. A platform that reaches more people and holds more first-party data can target and measure ads better, so advertisers pay more for the same impression - which funds more reach and more data. That feedback loop concentrates ad dollars inside a few 'walled gardens' (Google, Meta, Amazon) rather than spreading them across the open web.

companies.name: Meta
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: Forecast to pass Google for the first time in 2026. Earns almost all revenue from advertising across its apps.

companies.name: Google (Alphabet)
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: The long-time leader. Spans search ads (its biggest business) and YouTube video ads.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: The retail-media leader: ads placed next to shopping results, where buying intent is highest. The fastest-growing of the big three.

companies.name: ByteDance (TikTok, Douyin)
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: TikTok (4.8%) plus the Chinese app Douyin (3.1%), per eMarketer. The largest ad seller outside the US triopoly.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: About half from LinkedIn, the rest from Bing/Microsoft Advertising and the Xandr ad exchange (eMarketer).

companies.name: Apple
companies.share_basis: share of worldwide digital ad revenue, 2026 forecast (eMarketer)
companies.note: Mostly App Store Search Ads; small today but a lever on the whole market via its privacy controls on rivals' tracking.

products_note: Flagship ad products as of Nov 2026, checked against each company's ad documentation and 2025-2026 coverage; these are long-standing ad lines. Shares are eMarketer's April 2026 forecast of worldwide digital ad revenue; the six listed firms cover about 74%, with the remaining ~26% fragmented across open-web publishers, ad networks and regional players. NAICS 516210 is only an anchor - the sellers actually span search portals, social and media networks, and retail sites.
